newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police out in force to stop May Day clashes.
newsitem.headline: German police out in force to stop May Day clashes.

text.p: German police braced for violence on Thursday as thousands of demonstrators gathered across the country for traditonal Labour Day rallies.

Around 4,500 police were on duty to keep right and left apart in Leipzig, where trade unions were demonstrating and where the right-wing National Democratic Party of Germany (NPD) also planned to rally despite a ban by authorities.

Union protesters carried banners blaming Chancellor Helmut Kohl for the country's post-war record unemployment -- at 4.5 million in March. A picture of Kohl pointing outwards was accompanied by the words "We can save on you too!"
Berlin authorities also promised a heavy security presence and said police would not hesitate to use force if violence erupted.
Extremists in Berlin have targeted expensive cars, shops and bars in the past. They went on the rampage 10 years ago on May 1, setting fire to a supermarket.
Berlin authorities said they could not stop left-wing extremists from travelling to Leipzig but that police would try to make sure they were not carrying weapons.
Leipzig police said they had stopped around 140 right-wing and left-wing extremists from entering the city.

Oskar Lafontaine, leader of the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), and Klaus Zwickel, head of Germany's largest union IG Metall, were due to address the rally in Leipzig organised by the German Trade Union Federation (DGB).
Union members were expected to form a human chain around the centre of Leipzig to symbolise protecting the town from rising right-wing extremism.
